definition_zh: 宫殿；王宫；主教府；豪华宅邸；大型公共文化建筑
definition_en: the official residence of a king, queen, bishop or other high dignitary, or any very large and grand building
core_image: 一道正门通向铺石大院，院后是层层抬高的殿堂，每一层都比前一层更不容外人进入
scene: 铁门后是铺石大院，台阶一层层通向正殿。The palace opens its state rooms to visitors only two months a year.
sceneCN: 这里 palace 指「君主或高级显要的官邸」（第 1 个义项：王宫、宫殿）；句意为这座王宫每年只有两个月向访客开放国事厅。图中可辨识物件：铁门、铺石大院、台阶、正殿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 豪华大宅；大型公共建筑

derivatives.zh: 行宫领地；普法尔茨伯爵领地

senses.title: The residence of a ruler
senses.definition: the official home and ceremonial centre of a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 国王、女王或皇帝的官邸与礼仪中心
senses.example: The palace balcony faces the wide avenue where crowds gather.
senses.exampleCN: 王宫的阳台朝向人群聚集的宽阔大道。
senses.why: the word began as the name of one hill in Rome, then of the emperor's house on it, and finally of any ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是罗马一座山的名字，随后指山上皇帝的宅邸，最后泛指任何君主的宅邸。

senses.title: A bishop's residence
senses.definition: the official residence of a bishop or archbishop, often beside the cathedral
senses.definitionCN: 主教或大主教的官邸，常位于主教座堂旁
senses.example: The archbishop's palace shares a wall with the cathedral garden.
senses.exampleCN: 大主教府与主教座堂的花园共用一道墙。
senses.why: bishops held princely authority in many periods, so their houses took the same word as a king's.
senses.whyCN: 在许多时期主教握有诸侯般的权柄，因此他们的宅邸与国王用同一个词。

senses.title: A very grand private house
senses.definition: a private mansion large and ornate enough to seem royal
senses.definitionCN: 大到与华丽到看上去像王室居所的私人宅邸
senses.example: The merchant built a palace of brick beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那位商人在河边建了一座砖砌豪宅。
senses.why: wealth copies the forms of power, so a rich man's house borrows the name of a ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 财富会模仿权力的形式，因此富人的宅邸借用了君主居所的名字。

senses.title: A public palace of culture
senses.titleCN: 文化宫等大型公共建筑
senses.definition: a large state-built hall for culture, sport or exhibitions, common in former socialist countries
senses.definitionCN: 国家兴建的大型文化、体育或展览场馆，在旧社会主义国家常见
senses.example: The palace of culture has a theatre, a library and a swimming pool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座文化宫里有剧场、图书馆和游泳池。
senses.why: the state took the prestige of the palace and gave it to public leisure, so the word became civic.
senses.whyCN: 国家把宫殿的声望转给公共休闲，因此这个词变得市政化。

senses.title: Any lavish place
senses.definition: a building or room remarkable for comfort, size and expense
senses.definitionCN: 以舒适、宽敞与昂贵著称的建筑或房间
senses.example: The old cinema was a palace of red velvet and gilded plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老电影院是一座红丝绒与镀金灰泥的宫殿。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the splendour of the original, dropping the ruler entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留原义的富丽，把君主完全去掉了。

senses.title: The court as a government
senses.definition: the ruler's household and advisers, treated as a political actor
senses.definitionCN: 君主的家臣与顾问群体，被当作一个政治行为者
senses.example: The palace denied that the minister had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 王室方面否认那位大臣已被免职。
senses.why: reporters say 'the palace' when they mean the household that speaks for the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 记者说「王室」时，指的是替君主发声的那套家臣体系。

senses.title: The Palatine hill in Rome
senses.titleCN: 罗马帕拉蒂尼山上的宫殿
senses.definition: the imperial residence on the Palatine hill, whose name became the general word
senses.definitionCN: 帕拉蒂尼山上的皇帝居所，其名字成为通名
senses.example: The ruins of the palace overlook the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 宫殿废墟俯瞰着广场。
senses.why: one hill's name spread until every ruler's house in Europe carried it.
senses.whyCN: 一座山的名字扩散开来，直到欧洲每位君主的宅邸都带上了它。

senses.title: A movie palace
senses.definition: a large, lavishly decorated cinema of the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪初那种装饰华丽的大型电影院
senses.example: The movie palace seats two thousand under a painted sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电影宫在画出来的天空下可坐两千人。
senses.why: early cinemas sold an evening of luxury, so they named themselves after the most luxurious building they knew.
senses.whyCN: 早期影院卖的是一晚的奢华，因此用他们所知最奢华的建筑来命名自己。

intro.en: Palace is a place name before it is a building word: the Palatine hill in Rome gave its name to the emperor's house and then to grand houses everywhere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: palace 先是地名，后才是建筑词：罗马的帕拉蒂尼山把名字给了皇帝的宅邸，再给了各地的宏大宅邸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Palatium was the name of one of Rome's seven hills, where Augustus and later emperors built their residences.
items.cn: Palatium 是罗马七座山之一的名字，奥古斯都及后来的皇帝在此营建居所。

items.en: Because the emperor's house stood on that hill, the hill's name became a word for the house itself.
items.cn: 由于皇帝的宅邸立在那座山上，山名便成了指宅邸本身的词。

items.en: Old French palais carried the word into English, where it first named a royal residence.
items.cn: 古法语 palais 把该词带入英语，最初指王室居所。

items.en: In the Middle Ages the word widened to bishops' houses and then to any exceptionally grand town house.
items.cn: 中世纪时该词扩展到主教府，再扩展到任何格外宏大的城中宅邸。

items.en: In the twentieth century states built palaces of culture and workers' clubs, giving the word a public meaning.
items.cn: 二十世纪国家兴建文化宫与工人俱乐部，使这个词带上公共含义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of the hill name Palatium is disputed; a link to a shepherd god or to a word for a stake has been suggested, but neither is demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：山名 Palatium 的来源有争议；有人提出与牧神有关，或与表示「木桩」的词有关，但两者都未得到证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like palace or share its grand-house field but differ in origin; group two holds other grand residences.
note.cn: 第一组是与 palace 形近或同属「宏大宅邸」语义场、但来源不同的词；第二组是其他显赫居所。

entries.definition: Like a palace in size and splendour; it describes a quality and never names a building type.
entries.definitionCN: 在体量与富丽上像宫殿；描述一种性质，从不指建筑类型。

entries.definition: The domain of a count palatine, an official with royal powers in a border region; it names land and office.
entries.definitionCN: 宫廷伯爵的领地，指在边境地区拥有王权的官员辖区；指土地与职衔。

entries.definition: An Italian town house of a noble family; English borrowed it for a specific Mediterranean type.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利贵族家族的城中宅邸；英语借来表示一种特定的地中海类型。

entries.definition: A seizure of power by insiders close to the ruler; the phrase uses palace as the seat of power, not as architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 由君主身边内部人发动的夺权；短语把 palace 当作权力中心，而非建筑。

entries.definition: A fortified residence; it stresses defence, while a palace stresses display and administration.
entries.definitionCN: 设防的居所，强调防御；而 palace 强调展示与治理。

entries.definition: A very large private house; it lacks the royal or episcopal rank that palace implies.
entries.definitionCN: 极大型的私人住宅；缺少 palace 所含的王室或主教等级。

entries.definition: The neutral word for an official home, used when rank should not be emphasized.
entries.definitionCN: 指官邸的中性词，用于不宜强调等级时。

entries.definition: A French country house or estate; it combines castle and country house associations.
entries.definitionCN: 法国的乡间宅邸或庄园，兼有城堡与乡居宅邸的联想。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的山名、真实的等级词与真实的复合词。

normal.en: One hill in Rome gave its name to every royal house in Europe.
normal.cn: 罗马的一座山，把名字给了欧洲每一座王室宅邸。

normal.en: The family runs palace, palatial, palatinate, palazzo, palace coup.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 palace、palatial、palatinate、palazzo、palace coup。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: royal palace, archbishop's palace, palace of culture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：王宫、大主教府、文化宫。

normal.en: Rank decides the word: a bishop's house and a king's house can both be palaces.
normal.cn: 等级决定用词：主教的宅邸与国王的宅邸都可以叫 palace。

normal.en: The movie palace sold luxury by borrowing the most luxurious name available.
normal.cn: 电影宫借用了当时最奢华的名字来售卖奢华。

abstract.cn: 想象一座房子吞下了整座山，并把山名穿在身上。

examples.cn: 君主制结束后，这座王宫被改为博物馆开放。

examples.en: The archbishop's palace dates from the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 大主教府始建于十二世纪。

dict_mnemonic.text: Palatium（罗马帕拉蒂尼山）→ 山上皇帝宅邸 → 宫殿、豪华宅邸

root: 拉丁 Palatium 原为罗马七丘之一的名字，因皇帝宅邸建于其上而转指宫殿；经古法语 palais 入英语。山名本身的来源不确定。英语 palace。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one address: a ruler's house on a hill becomes a bishop's house, a rich man's house, a public hall, a metaphor, a government, a ruin and a cinema.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个住处展开：山上的君主宅邸成为主教府、富商大宅、公共厅堂、比喻、政府、废墟与影院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gate, courtyard, stair and inner hall, each layer admitting fewer people than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：门、院、阶、内殿，每一层允许进入的人都比前一层更少。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL HOUSE: the hill name became the emperor's residence, and that residence became the general word.
branches.cn: 最初的宅邸：山名成为皇帝居所之名，那座居所又成为通名。

branches.en: PRINCELY CLERGY: a bishop's house takes the royal word because bishops held princely power.
branches.cn: 诸侯般的主教：主教府沿用王室用词，因为主教握有诸侯般的权力。

branches.en: WEALTH COPIES POWER: a merchant's mansion and a lavish hotel borrow palace's splendour without a ruler.
branches.cn: 财富模仿权力：富商豪宅与豪华旅馆借走了 palace 的富丽，却不要君主。

branches.en: PUBLIC SPLENDOUR: the state builds palaces of culture, and cinemas call themselves movie palaces.
branches.cn: 公共的富丽：国家兴建文化宫，影院则自称电影宫。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the building's name moves to the people who speak for the ruler.
branches.cn: 家臣体系：建筑之名转到替君主发声的那群人身上。

intro.en: Palace has no prefix or suffix of its own: it is a place name that became a noun, and its derived words are built on that noun.
intro.cn: palace 本身没有前缀或后缀：它是一个变成名词的地名，其派生词都建在这个名词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin Palatium supplied the name, and the adjective palatinus described what belonged to the imperial hill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Palatium 提供了这个名字，形容词 palatinus 描述属于皇帝那座山的事物。

definition_zh: 苍白的；浅色的；逊色的；变苍白
definition_en: having little colour in the face, light and weak in shade, less impressive than something it is compared with, and to lose colour
core_image: 一张血色退去的脸，像被水冲淡的颜色
scene: 清晨的诊室里，医生抬起病人的手腕，看那张几乎没有血色的脸。The nurse noticed how pale his face had become after the long night.
sceneCN: 这里 pale 是「脸色苍白」（第 1 个义项：脸上缺少血色）；句意为护士注意到他熬过漫长一夜之后脸色变得多么苍白。图中可辨识物件：诊室的灯、病人的手腕、床尾的病历夹。

pale 加副词后缀 -ly，指苍白地、淡淡地

与 pale 同出拉丁词干 pallidus，指无血色的、病态的苍白

senses.title: Having little colour in the face
senses.definition: having less colour than usual in the face, often because of illness, fear or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 脸上比平时缺少血色，常因生病、害怕或疲惫
senses.example: She went pale when the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。
senses.why: Latin pallere meant to be pale, and the word has always started from skin losing its healthy colour, so the face is its oldest and most natural subject.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pallere 本义就是发白、失色，这个词最早说的是皮肤失去健康颜色，所以「脸」是它最古老也最自然的落点。

senses.title: Light and weak in shade
senses.definition: of a colour or light, close to white and not strong or deep
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色或光线接近白色，不浓、不深
senses.example: The walls were painted a pale grey.
senses.exampleCN: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。
senses.why: Once the word names a weak version of white, it can describe any colour that has been diluted, which is why pale blue sits nearer white than pure blue.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用来指「被冲淡的白」，就能描述任何掺淡的颜色，所以 pale blue 比纯蓝更靠近白。

senses.title: Weaker than what it is compared with
senses.definition: less impressive, less strong or less real than another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 比同类的另一事物更不打动人、更弱或更不真实
senses.example: The new version is a pale imitation of the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新版本只是对旧版本一种拙劣的模仿。
senses.why: A pale copy lacks the full colour of the original, so the word came to mean anything that looks washed out beside a stronger model.
senses.whyCN: 淡色的复制品没有原件那样饱满的颜色，于是这个词转指任何在更强的样本旁显得褪色、单薄的东西。

senses.title: To lose colour from the face
senses.definition: to become pale, especially in the face, or to make something seem less strong by comparison
senses.definitionCN: 变得苍白，尤指脸色发白；也可指使某物相形之下显得黯淡
senses.example: His cheeks paled at the sight of the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 一看见血，他的双颊就白了。
senses.why: The verb only sets the adjective in motion: the colour leaves the face while others watch it go, so the change itself becomes the event.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把形容词动了起来：血色在旁人眼前从脸上退走，于是「退去」这个变化本身成了一件可以叙述的事。

intro.en: Pale comes from Latin pallere, to be pale, through Old French; the same Latin family gives pallor and pallid, so the colour sense is very old.
intro.cn: pale 出自拉丁语 pallere（发白），经古法语进入英语；同一拉丁词族还给出 pallor 与 pallid，颜色义由来已久。

items.en: The verb pallere meant to be pale or to look colourless, and it described the skin before it described anything else.
items.cn: 动词 pallere 意为发白、没有血色，它最初描述的是皮肤，而不是别的物体。

items.en: Its adjective pallidus meant pale or wan and passed into learned words such as pallid.
items.cn: 它的形容词 pallidus 意为苍白、憔悴，后来进入 pallid 这类书面词。

items.en: Old French turned the Latin adjective into pale, and the form crossed to England with Norman French.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词写成 pale，这个形式随诺曼法语一起进入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English used pale for a face without colour and, by extension, for light and washed-out shades.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pale 指没有血色的脸，并由此延伸到浅淡、发白的颜色。

items.en: Modern English keeps paler and palest as the comparison, and adds the figurative sense of a weak or faded copy.
items.cn: 现代英语用 paler 与 palest 作比较级和最高级，并增加了「逊色、褪色的复制品」这一比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the learned relatives that keep the Latin colour stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for a face or a shade that has lost its strength.
note.cn: 形近组收保留拉丁颜色词干的书面亲属词；近义组收描述失去强度的脸色与色调的词。

entries.definition: Pale and unhealthy, especially of a face; it keeps the Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而病态的，尤指脸色；保留了拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being pale, used mostly in medical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的状态，多用于医学文字。

entries.definition: The quality of being pale; pale plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的性质；pale 加 -ness。

entries.definition: The colour of fresh snow or milk, the lightest shade there is.
entries.definitionCN: 新雪或牛奶的颜色，最浅的色调。

entries.definition: Pale and tired-looking, as if from illness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而疲惫的，像病后那样。

entries.definition: Pale grey, like ash, usually of a frightened face.
entries.definitionCN: 灰白的，像灰烬一样，常形容受惊的脸。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for being pale, and everything else in the family returns to a colour that has been drained.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「发白」的动词上，词族里其余的词都回到一种被抽走浓度的颜色。

normal.en: Latin pallere means to be pale, so the word begins at the skin, not at the paint pot.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pallere 意为发白，所以这个词的起点在皮肤，而不在油漆桶。

normal.en: Pallor and pallid are learned relatives that keep the Latin colour sense.
normal.cn: pallor 与 pallid 是保留拉丁颜色义的书面亲属词。

normal.en: A face goes pale, a colour is pale, and a copy looks pale beside the original: one word measures distance from full colour.
normal.cn: 脸会发白，颜色会发淡，复制品在原件旁显得褪色，同一个词量的是离饱满颜色有多远。

normal.en: The verb pale is simply the adjective set in motion while others watch the colour leave.
normal.cn: 动词 pale 只是把形容词动起来，让别人看着颜色退走。

normal.en: Pale blue is not a kind of blue but blue with white mixed in, which is why the word can also mean weak.
normal.cn: pale blue 不是一种蓝，而是掺了白的蓝，所以这个词也能表示「弱」。

abstract.en: Colour is evidence of health, so losing it is the body's first way of saying that something is wrong.
abstract.cn: 颜色是健康的证据，褪色是身体最先说出「不对劲」的方式。

abstract.en: A pale copy is judged against an original it cannot match, which turns the word into a quiet comparison.
abstract.cn: 淡色的复制品总被拿去和配不上的原件相比，这个词因此成了一场安静的对照。

abstract.en: Every pale thing is a full thing with part of its colour taken away.
abstract.cn: 每个发淡的东西，都是被抽走了一部分颜色的完整之物。

examples.en: She went pale when the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。

examples.en: The walls were painted a pale grey.
examples.cn: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。

examples.en: The sequel is a pale copy of the original film.
examples.cn: 这部续集是原片一个褪色的复制品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪」——病人脸色苍白，床边总得有人陪着；记住 pale 是苍白。

root: 拉丁语 pallere（发白）— pallidus（苍白的）— 古法语 pale — 英语 pale；同族书面词有 pallor、pallid。

sensesIntro.en: The core is colour with its strength taken out; the senses move from the face, to light shades, to the figurative weak copy, and finally to the act of losing colour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被抽走浓度的颜色；义项从脸，到浅淡的色彩，再到比喻性的「逊色复制品」，最后回到「失去颜色」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face whose colour has drained away like paint thinned by water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张血色退去的脸，颜色像被水冲淡的颜料。

branches.en: a patient's face under a clinic lamp
branches.cn: 诊室灯下病人的脸

branches.en: a wall painted a soft grey
branches.cn: 被刷成柔和浅灰的墙

branches.en: a sequel that cannot match the first film
branches.cn: 比不过首部的续集

branches.en: cheeks losing colour at the sight of blood
branches.cn: 见到血时退去血色的脸颊

branches.en: a washed-out colour and a washed-out copy
branches.cn: 褪掉的颜色与褪掉的复制品

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of being pale, its adjective and noun, and English suffixes that turn the quality into a state or a manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示发白的动词及其形容词、名词承载，再加上把性质变成状态或方式的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: a verb of being pale, an adjective for the pale colour, and a noun for paleness itself.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族有明确记录：表示发白的动词、指苍白颜色的形容词，以及指苍白本身的名词。

items.meaning: to be pale, to lack colour

definition_zh: 古生物学家；从事化石发掘与研究者；博物馆古生物部门的研究或策展人员
definition_en: a person who studies ancient life through fossils, whether in the field, a museum or a laboratory
core_image: 野外营地里，研究者蹲在碎石堆前，用镊子夹起一颗牙齿化石放进编号袋
scene: 野外营地里，一位研究者蹲在碎石堆中，用镊子夹起一颗牙齿化石放进编号袋。 The paleontologist brushed sand from a tooth before it could crack.
sceneCN: 这里 paleontologist 指「从事古生物研究的专业人员」（第 1 个义项：以化石研究远古生命的学者）；句意为这位古生物学家在一颗牙齿开裂之前把沙刷掉。图中可辨识物件：碎石堆、镊子、牙齿化石、编号袋、记录本。

pos.zh: 古生物学家；古生物研究者；古生物部门的研究或策展人员

collocations.zh: 古生物学家用的地质锤

senses.title: A specialist in ancient life
senses.titleCN: 研究远古生命的专业学者
senses.definition: a scientist who studies extinct organisms and their environments through fossil evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过化石证据研究已灭绝生物及其环境的科学家
senses.example: The paleontologist compared the jaw with three museum specimens.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家把这件下颌与三件馆藏标本作了比较。
senses.why: the agent suffix -ist marks the person, while the discipline noun marks the field, so the pair is strictly complementary.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -ist 标出人，学科名词标出领域，两者严格互补。

senses.title: A field collector
senses.definition: a person who finds, excavates and records fossils at outcrops and quarries
senses.definitionCN: 在露头与采石场寻找、发掘并记录化石的人
senses.example: The paleontologist spent six weeks mapping the quarry before digging.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家在动土前花了六周测绘采坑。
senses.why: fieldwork is a distinct role within the profession, and the same title covers the person holding the trowel.
senses.whyCN: 野外工作是这一行中独立的角色，同一个头衔也指拿着小铲的人。

senses.title: A museum curator or researcher
senses.titleCN: 博物馆的古生物研究或策展人员
senses.definition: a specialist employed by a museum to care for, study and display fossil collections
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于博物馆，负责保管、研究与展示化石藏品的人员
senses.example: The paleontologist rehoused the type specimens in acid-free trays.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家把模式标本改放到无酸托盘里。
senses.why: institutions use the title for curatorial work, which is research plus stewardship rather than excavation.
senses.whyCN: 机构用这个头衔指策展工作，即研究加上保管，而非发掘。

senses.title: A university researcher
senses.definition: an academic who teaches the subject and runs a research programme on fossil material
senses.definitionCN: 教授该学科并就化石材料主持研究项目的学者
senses.example: The paleontologist supervised two doctoral students on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家在该项目上指导两名博士生。
senses.why: the title attaches to a post as much as to a person, so it appears in staffing lists and grant applications.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔既属于人也属于职位，因此出现在人员名单与经费申请中。

senses.title: A consultant on stratigraphy
senses.titleCN: 为地层工作提供咨询的专家
senses.definition: a specialist called in to identify fossils so that a rock unit can be dated or correlated
senses.definitionCN: 被请来鉴定化石，以便给岩层定年或对比的专家
senses.example: The paleontologist identified the graptolites that fixed the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家鉴定了确定该阶的笔石。
senses.why: industry and survey work employ the title for a service role, where the fossil is evidence rather than an object of wonder.
senses.whyCN: 工业与地质调查用这个头衔指服务性角色，此时化石是证据而非观赏对象。

senses.title: An amateur specialist
senses.definition: an informed non-professional who collects and studies fossils seriously outside paid employment
senses.definitionCN: 在职业之外认真采集与研究化石的非专业者
senses.example: An amateur paleontologist found the site while walking a new road cut.
senses.exampleCN: 一位业余古生物研究者在查看新开的公路切面时发现了这个地点。
senses.why: the qualification here is knowledge and practice, not salary, which is why the same noun serves both worlds.
senses.whyCN: 这里的资格是知识与实践，而非薪俸，因此同一名词服务于两个世界。

senses.title: A science communicator
senses.titleCN: 从事科普的古生物学者
senses.definition: a specialist who explains fossil research to the public through writing, media or museum tours
senses.definitionCN: 通过写作、媒体或博物馆导览向公众解释化石研究的专家
senses.example: As a paleontologist, she writes as carefully for children as for journals.
senses.exampleCN: 作为古生物学家，她为儿童写作和为期刊写作一样用心。
senses.why: public-facing work has become part of the role, so the title now covers speaking as well as studying.
senses.whyCN: 面向公众的工作已成为角色的一部分，因此这个头衔也涵盖讲述，而不仅是研究。

senses.title: A named branch specialist
senses.titleCN: 某一分支的古生物学家
senses.definition: a specialist identified by the group studied, as in vertebrate paleontologist or palynologist
senses.definitionCN: 以所研究类群来限定的专家，如脊椎动物古生物学家或孢粉学家
senses.example: The vertebrate paleontologist joined the excavation for one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这位脊椎动物古生物学家参加了一季的发掘。
senses.why: branch names combine with the person noun, so the title scales from the whole field down to a single group.
senses.whyCN: 分支名与人物名词组合，使头衔可以从整个领域细到单一类群。

intro.en: Paleontologist is paleontology plus the agent suffix -ist, from Greek -istēs. The discipline name was coined in the early nineteenth century; the personal noun followed immediately. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: paleontologist 是 paleontology 加施事后缀 -ist（源自希腊 -istēs）。学科名于十九世纪初造出，人物名词紧随其后。年代均为约数。

items.en: Paleontology joins palaios 'old', onta 'beings' and -logia 'study'; the discipline name was assembled in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: paleontology 由 palaios「古老」、onta「存在者」与 -logia「研究」组合；学科名于十九世纪初拼成。

items.en: -ist comes from Greek -istēs, a suffix of persons who practise or adhere to something, as in botanist and geologist.
items.cn: -ist 来自希腊 -istēs，指从事或信奉某事的人，如 botanist 与 geologist。

items.en: Once the field had a name, its practitioner was formed by adding -ist, and both spellings palaeo- and paleo- carry the pair.
items.cn: 领域一有名称，从业者便通过加 -ist 构成，palaeo- 与 paleo- 两种拼写都带这一对词。

items.en: As museums and universities created posts in the nineteenth century, the title became an office as well as a description.
items.cn: 随着博物馆与大学在十九世纪设立岗位，这个头衔既成描述也成职位。

items.en: Twentieth-century practice extended the title to amateurs and communicators who publish serious work without a salary.
items.cn: 二十世纪的实践把这个头衔扩展到无薪却发表严肃工作的业余者与科普者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): the suffix and stems are secure, but the earliest use of the personal noun is dated approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：后缀与词干确定，但人物名词的最早使用只能约略定年。

note.en: Group one separates the person noun from the field and from look-alike titles; group two separates it from neighbouring professions.
note.cn: 第一组把人物名词与学科名及形近头衔分开；第二组区分它与相邻职业。

entries.definition: The discipline; the person noun differs only by the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 学科；人物名词只差一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: The same profession written with ae, standard in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业，用 ae 拼写，通行于英国。

entries.definition: A specialist in ancient humans only; the wider title covers all extinct life.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究远古人类的专家；较宽的头衔涵盖一切已灭绝生命。

entries.definition: A specialist in fossil plants; the wider title does not require plants.
entries.definitionCN: 研究化石植物的专家；较宽的头衔并不限于植物。

entries.definition: A specialist in past human societies through material traces; the two trades overlap at sites but differ in object.
entries.definitionCN: 通过物质遗存研究过去人类社会的专家；两者在遗址上交叉，但对象不同。

entries.definition: A specialist in rocks and earth history; fossils are one kind of evidence among many.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地球历史的专家；化石只是众多证据之一。

entries.definition: Someone who gathers fossils, often without publishing; the title implies study, not just acquisition.
entries.definitionCN: 采集化石的人，常常并不发表；后者含研究之意，不只是收集。

entries.definition: A person responsible for a collection; a paleontologist may be one, but curation is the duty, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 负责藏品的人；古生物学家可以担任，但策展是职责，而非学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paleontology + -ist: the person who practises the study of ancient beings.
normal.cn: paleontology + -ist：从事远古存在者研究的人。

normal.en: The title pairs with the field noun exactly: paleontology/paleontologist.
normal.cn: 这个头衔与学科名词严格配对：paleontology/paleontologist。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the vowel: palaeontologist.
normal.cn: 英式拼写多一个元音：palaeontologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field paleontologist, museum paleontologist, vertebrate paleontologist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外古生物学家、博物馆古生物学家、脊椎动物古生物学家。

normal.en: Compare archaeologist and geologist: same site, different object.
normal.cn: 比较 archaeologist 与 geologist：同一遗址，不同对象。

abstract.en: Picture a person kneeling in dust with a brush and a numbered bag.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人跪在尘土里，拿着刷子和编号袋。

abstract.en: Picture a jaw on a table with three labels around it and a lamp overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一件下颌，周围三个标签，头顶一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a child on a museum floor asking a patient expert why the bone is heavy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子坐在博物馆地上，问一位耐心的专家骨头为什么这么重。

examples.en: The paleontologist published the jaw as a new genus.
examples.cn: 这位古生物学家把这件下颌发表为一个新属。

examples.en: Two paleontologists spent the winter preparing the slab.
examples.cn: 两位古生物学家花了一个冬天修整这块板岩。

examples.en: As a paleontologist, he refused to identify the bone from a photograph.
examples.cn: 作为古生物学家，他拒绝仅凭照片鉴定这块骨头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paleonto（古生物）+ logist（学者）」——研究古生物的学者 → 古生物学家

root: paleontology（希腊 palaios「古老」+ onta「存在者」+ -logia「研究」）+ 施事后缀 -ist（希腊 -istēs）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one person in different hats: specialist, digger, curator, academic, consultant, amateur, explainer and branch expert.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描写同一个人戴的不同帽子：专家、发掘者、策展人、学者、顾问、业余者、讲述者与分支专家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone kneeling in dust with a brush, a bag and a label.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跪在尘土中，身边是刷子、袋子和标签。

branches.en: THE PERSON AT WORK: the title covers both the specialist and the trowel.
branches.cn: 工作中的这个人：头衔兼指专家与拿小铲的人。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL HATS: museum stewardship and academic posts.
branches.cn: 机构中的帽子：博物馆保管与大学教职。

branches.en: SERVICE ROLE: identifying fossils so that rock can be dated.
branches.cn: 服务角色：鉴定化石以便给岩层定年。

branches.en: BEYOND SALARY: amateurs and public explainers practise the same trade.
branches.cn: 薪俸之外：业余者与科普者从事同一行当。

branches.en: NAMED SPECIALITY: the title narrows to a group, as in vertebrate paleontologist.
branches.cn: 命名的专长：头衔可窄到某一类群，如脊椎动物古生物学家。

intro.en: Paleontologist is the field noun plus the Greek agent suffix -ist, so the whole word unpacks as the person of the discipline.
intro.cn: paleontologist 是学科名词加希腊施事后缀 -ist，整词可解作「该学科的人」。

latinIntro.en: Greek palaios, onta and -logia supply the field; -istēs, through -ist, supplies the person. Latin has no part in the word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 palaios、onta 与 -logia 提供领域义；-istēs 经 -ist 提供人物义。拉丁语不参与此词构成。

items.example: The prefix fixes the time depth.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀固定了时间深度。

items.example: The stem fixes the object studied.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干固定了研究对象。
古生物学先给领域命名。

items.example: The argument rests on paleontological detail.
items.exampleCN: 该论证依赖古生物学的细节。
一位古人类学家加入了调查。
古植物学家鉴定了这片叶子。

definition_zh: 手掌；掌心；棕榈树；把…藏于掌中；骗卖
definition_en: the inner surface of the hand, a tropical tree with a crown of large fanning leaves, and to hide something small in the hand or pass it off on someone
core_image: 一只摊开的手，掌纹向四周散开，像撑开的扇叶
scene: 庙会的老先生摊开手，让围着的孩子看他掌心的纹路。The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
sceneCN: 这里 palm 是「手掌、掌心」（第 1 个义项：手的内侧面）；句意为老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。图中可辨识物件：摊开的手掌、庙会的灯笼、围观的孩子。

collocations.phrase: in the palm of one's hand
collocations.zh: 在某人的掌心里；完全受其掌控

derivatives.zh: palm 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist，指看手相的人
palm 加表示技艺的后缀 -istry，指看手相的方术
palm 加 -y 构成，先指多棕榈的，再引申为繁荣兴旺的

senses.title: The inner surface of the hand
senses.definition: the inner surface of the hand, from the wrist to the base of the fingers
senses.definitionCN: 手的内侧面，从手腕一直到手指根部
senses.example: The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
senses.exampleCN: 老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。
senses.why: Latin palma first named this flat, open surface, so the word begins at the body part whenever a hand is held out or turned upward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 palma 最初就指这块平坦、张开的表面，所以只要把手摊开或翻向上，这个词就从身体部位开始。

senses.title: A tropical tree with fanning leaves
senses.definition: a tropical tree with a tall trunk and a crown of large leaves spreading from one point
senses.definitionCN: 一种热带树木，树干高大，大叶子从同一点向四周展开
senses.example: A row of palms shaded the road along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸公路旁一排棕榈树投下阴凉。
senses.why: The fronds of many palms spread from one point like the fingers of an open hand, so Latin reused palma for the tree and English kept both senses.
senses.whyCN: 许多棕榈的叶片从同一点向外张开，像摊开的手指向四周，拉丁语就把 palma 也给了这种树，英语把两个义项都留了下来。

senses.title: To hide something in the hand
senses.definition: to hide a small object in the closed hand, especially to deceive someone
senses.definitionCN: 把一个小东西藏在合起的手里，尤指为了骗人
senses.example: He palmed the coin and slipped it into his sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 他把硬币扣在掌心，顺手滑进了袖口。
senses.why: Once palm names the part of the hand others cannot see when it closes, the verb can name the trick of keeping an object there while everyone watches.
senses.whyCN: 既然 palm 指手合拢后别人看不见的那一面，动词就能指「在众目之下把东西留在那里」的手法。

senses.title: To pass something off on someone
senses.definition: to get rid of something by persuading someone that it is better than it is
senses.definitionCN: 靠让人相信某物比实际更好，从而把东西脱手
senses.example: The dealer palmed off a fake watch on a tourist.
senses.exampleCN: 那个商贩把一块假表骗卖给了游客。
senses.why: The hand that conceals can also pass something on unseen, so palm off names a deal finished before the other person has had a proper look.
senses.whyCN: 会藏东西的手也能把东西悄悄递出去，所以 palm off 指一笔在对方看清之前就已成交的买卖。

intro.en: Palm goes back to Latin palma, which named both the flat of the hand and the tree whose leaves spread like fingers; Old English borrowed it for the tree and the hand.
intro.cn: palm 出自拉丁语 palma，这个词既指手掌的平面，也指叶片像手指一样张开的树；古英语把两个意思都借了进来。

items.en: Palma named the flat inner surface of the hand, the part held open or used to strike.
items.cn: palma 指手内那一块平坦的表面，也就是摊开或用来拍打的那一面。

items.en: The same word was given to the date palm because its fronds fan out from one point like an open hand.
items.cn: 同一个词也被给了枣椰树，因为它的叶丛从同一点张开，像一只摊开的手。

items.en: Old English took the word through the church, first for the palm branches carried on Palm Sunday and then for the tree.
items.cn: 古英语经教会借入这个词，先指棕枝主日所持的棕榈枝，再指这种树。

items.en: Middle English kept the hand sense and the tree sense side by side, and also used palm as a unit of length taken from the hand.
items.cn: 中古英语让「手」与「树」两个义项并存，还把 palm 用作以手宽为准的长度单位。

items.en: Modern English keeps palmed and palming, and the phrase palm off for passing something off on someone.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 palmed 与 palming，以及表示「骗卖、塞给别人」的 palm off。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for the hand and the tree; the near-meaning group gathers words for hands and for the leaves that look like them.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语中兼指手掌与棕榈的那个词展开；近义组收表示手以及像手的叶片的词。

entries.definition: A medieval pilgrim who carried a palm branch home from the Holy Land.
entries.definitionCN: 中世纪从圣地朝圣归来、手持棕榈枝的朝圣者。

entries.definition: A person who reads the lines of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 看手相的人。

entries.definition: The practice of telling a person's future from the lines of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 从手掌纹路推测命运的方术。

entries.definition: The whole part of the body at the end of the arm, fingers included.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端包含手指的整个部位。

entries.definition: The foot of an animal such as a dog or cat.
entries.definitionCN: 狗、猫等动物的脚掌。

entries.definition: A long leaf of a palm or a fern, divided into many parts.
entries.definitionCN: 棕榈或蕨类那种分成许多部分的长叶。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word covers the open hand and the tree that copies its shape, and the family around it keeps folding the hand into a tool of hiding.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁词同时覆盖摊开的手与模仿其形状的树，而它周围的词族不断把这只手折成藏东西的工具。

normal.en: Latin palma is both the open hand and the palm tree, one picture doing two jobs.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 palma 既是摊开的手，也是棕榈树，一幅画面干了两件事。

normal.en: The lines of the palm are what palmistry claims to read.
normal.cn: 掌纹正是 palmistry 声称要读的东西。

normal.en: A palm was once a unit of length measured across the hand.
normal.cn: palm 曾是以手宽丈量的长度单位。

normal.en: The verb palm keeps the hand closed: the coin vanishes inside it.
normal.cn: 动词 palm 让手合起来：硬币就在里面不见了。

normal.en: Palm off adds a direction to that closed hand: the hidden thing is pushed onto someone else.
normal.cn: palm off 给这只合起的手加了方向：藏着的东西被推给了别人。

abstract.en: The palm is the part of the body that can both give and conceal.
abstract.cn: 手掌是身体上既能给予又能藏匿的那一部分。

abstract.en: A tree that looks like an open hand ties the body to the landscape.
abstract.cn: 一棵看起来像摊开的手的树，把身体和风景系在一起。

abstract.en: Whatever fits inside a closed palm is small enough to be denied.
abstract.cn: 能握进掌心的东西，小到可以否认它存在。

examples.en: The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
examples.cn: 老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。

examples.en: A row of palms shaded the road along the coast.
examples.cn: 海岸公路旁一排棕榈树投下阴凉。

examples.en: The dealer palmed off a fake watch on a tourist.
examples.cn: 那个商贩把一块假表骗卖给了游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕姆」——摊开手掌喊一声「帕姆」，记住 palm 是手掌。

root: 拉丁语 palma（手掌），同一个词又指棕榈，因叶丛像摊开的手；经古英语 palm 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the open hand; the senses widen to the tree that copies its shape, then narrow to the closed hand that hides and finally to the hand that cheats.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是摊开的手；义项先扩到形状如手的棕榈，再收拢到藏东西的合掌，最后落到行骗的那只手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand whose lines spread outward like the leaves of a fan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手，掌纹向四周散开，像撑开的扇叶。

branches.en: a reader tracing the lines of a palm
branches.cn: 看相人沿掌纹描过去

branches.en: a coast road shaded by tall palms
branches.cn: 被高大棕榈遮荫的海岸公路

branches.en: a coin vanishing inside a closed hand
branches.cn: 硬币在合起的手里消失

branches.en: a fake watch passed to a tourist
branches.cn: 假表被塞给游客

branches.en: leaves that fan out like fingers and a hand that closes
branches.cn: 像手指张开的叶丛与合拢的手

intro.en: The word is a single Latin noun for hand and tree, with English suffixes building the reader, the art and the tree-filled place.
intro.cn: 这个词就是一个兼指手掌与棕榈的拉丁名词，英语后缀在它周围造出看相人、相术和长满棕榈的地方。

latinIntro.en: Latin palma is recorded for both the hand and the tree, and the adjective palmatus describes something shaped or decorated like a hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 palma 兼指手掌与棕榈，形容词 palmatus 则描述像手一样张开或以棕榈装饰的东西。

shaped like a hand, decorated with palms

definition_zh: 恐慌；惊慌；经济恐慌；惊慌失措
definition_en: a sudden overpowering fear that stops clear thought, a widespread fright in a market or crowd, and to act in such fear
core_image: 灯忽然灭掉的剧场里，人群同时转身挤向同一个门口
scene: 剧场里的灯忽然全灭，前排的人先站起来，后排跟着往门口挤。A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
sceneCN: 这里 panic 是「群体性恐慌」（第 1 个义项：骤然袭来的强烈恐惧）；句意为后排的一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。图中可辨识物件：熄灭的顶灯、挤向出口的人影、翻倒的座椅。

derivatives.zh: panic 加 -y 构成，指容易惊慌的、慌慌张张的
panic 加 -ed 构成，指惊慌失措的
panic 与 stricken 复合而成，指被恐慌击中的

senses.title: A sudden overpowering fear
senses.definition: a sudden, overwhelming feeling of fear that stops people from thinking clearly
senses.definitionCN: 骤然袭来、压倒一切的恐惧，使人无法清楚思考
senses.example: A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
senses.exampleCN: 后排一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。
senses.why: The word comes from the god Pan, whose sudden cries in the hills were said to terrify travellers, so the sense begins with fear that arrives with no visible cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自牧神潘，据说他在山野里突然发出的叫声会让旅人惊恐，所以词义一开始就是「找不到明确来由的骤然恐惧」。

senses.title: A widespread fright in a market
senses.definition: a sudden loss of confidence that makes many people sell, withdraw or flee at the same moment
senses.definitionCN: 信心骤然崩塌，使许多人在同一时刻抛售、取钱或逃离
senses.example: A rumour about the bank set off a panic among small savers.
senses.exampleCN: 关于那家银行的传言在小储户中引发了一场恐慌。
senses.why: When many people feel the same sudden fear, the word moves from one heart to a whole market: everyone runs at once, and the running itself makes the danger worse.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时感到同一种骤然的恐惧，这个词就从一颗心移到一个市场：所有人一起奔跑，而奔跑本身又让危险更大。

senses.title: To act with blind fear
senses.definition: to be so frightened that you act without thinking, or to make other people behave that way
senses.definitionCN: 害怕到不假思索地行动，或使别人也这样行动
senses.example: She panicked when she could not find her passport at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 在登机口找不到护照时，她一下子慌了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into behaviour: the fear takes over the body, and the flailing that follows is the word in action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词变成行为：恐惧接管了身体，随后那阵手忙脚乱就是这个词的具体样子。

intro.en: Panic comes from the Greek god Pan; a sudden terror in lonely places was called panikon deima, the fear sent by Pan, and the word reached English through French.
intro.cn: panic 来自希腊牧神潘；荒野中骤然袭来的恐惧被称作 panikon deima，即「潘送来的恐惧」，这个词经法语进入英语。

items.en: Pan was the god of shepherds and wild country, and a sudden cry in the hills was said to come from him.
items.cn: 潘是牧人与荒野之神，山间突然响起的叫声被说成是他发出的。

items.en: Greek panikon, short for panikon deima, named the sudden terror that seized travellers in lonely places.
items.cn: 希腊语 panikon 是 panikon deima 的简称，指在荒野中突然攫住旅人的恐惧。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as panicus; it is a loan, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 panicus；这是借词，不是拉丁语固有词。

items.en: French panique carried the word into English, where it first named fear without a visible cause.
items.cn: 法语 panique 把这个词带进英语，最初指找不到可见原因的恐惧。

items.en: Modern English uses panic for personal fear and for market runs, and spells the past tense panicked with a k to keep the hard sound.
items.cn: 现代英语用 panic 指个人恐惧与市场挤兑，过去式写作 panicked，加 k 以保住硬音。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the English forms built on this noun; the near-meaning group gathers other names for intense fear.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个名词所造的英语形式展开；近义组收其他表示强烈恐惧的说法。

entries.definition: Easily frightened and unable to stay calm; panic plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 容易受惊、无法保持镇定的；panic 加 -y。

entries.definition: Seized by panic, or the past tense of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 被恐慌攫住的，或动词的过去式。

entries.definition: Overcome by panic, often used of a crowd or a face.
entries.definitionCN: 被恐慌击中的，常形容人群或脸色。

entries.definition: The general feeling that danger is near.
entries.definitionCN: 感到危险临近的普遍情绪。

entries.definition: Very great fear, stronger and longer than a fright.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的恐惧，比一时的惊吓更强也更久。

entries.definition: Sudden fear caused by a real or expected danger.
entries.definitionCN: 由真实或预期危险引起的骤然恐惧。

entries.definition: A short, sharp feeling of fear.
entries.definitionCN: 短促而尖锐的惊吓。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the name of a god and the shape of a Greek phrase, and its English forms have to protect one hard sound.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一位神的名字和一句希腊短语的形状，它的英语形式还得护住一个硬音。

normal.en: Pan was said to shout in lonely hills, and panic still means fear with no visible cause.
normal.cn: 据说潘会在荒野里突然叫喊，而 panic 至今仍指找不到可见原因的恐惧。

normal.en: The Greek phrase was panikon deima, the terror of Pan, and English cut it down to one word.
normal.cn: 希腊短语是 panikon deima，即「潘的恐惧」，英语把它压缩成了一个词。

normal.en: Panicked doubles the k so the c keeps its hard sound, unlike the wrong spelling paniced.
normal.cn: panicked 双写 k，让 c 保持硬音，而错误的拼写 paniced 做不到。

normal.en: Panic buying empties shelves before the storm has even arrived.
normal.cn: 恐慌性抢购在风暴还没到之前就把货架清空了。

normal.en: A panic attack is the old flight response running with nothing to run from.
normal.cn: 恐慌发作是古老的逃跑反应在空转，根本没有东西可逃。

abstract.en: Panic is fear that spreads faster than the news that caused it.
abstract.cn: 恐慌是一种比引发它的消息传得更快的恐惧。

abstract.en: A crowd in panic is many people obeying the same blind instruction.
abstract.cn: 陷入恐慌的人群，是许多人在服从同一条看不见的指令。

abstract.en: The god is gone, but the sudden shout in the hills is still inside the word.
abstract.cn: 神已经不在了，但山间那声骤然的喊叫仍留在这个词里。

examples.en: A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
examples.cn: 后排一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。

examples.en: A rumour about the bank set off a panic among small savers.
examples.cn: 关于那家银行的传言在小储户中引发了一场恐慌。

examples.en: She panicked when she could not find her passport at the gate.
examples.cn: 在登机口找不到护照时，她一下子慌了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你咳」——一慌就怕你咳出声来，越慌越乱；记住 panic 是恐慌。

root: 希腊神话牧神潘（Pan）；希腊语 panikon deima 意为「潘带来的恐惧」，经晚期拉丁语 panicus、法语 panique 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is fear with no clear cause; the senses spread from one person's sudden terror to a whole market running, and then to the behaviour that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是找不到明确来由的恐惧；义项从一个人的骤然惊恐，扩到整个市场的奔逃，再落到随之而来的失控行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a theatre going dark and a crowd turning toward one door at the same instant.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯灭的剧场里，人群在同一瞬间转身挤向同一扇门。

branches.en: a theatre darkening without warning
branches.cn: 没有预兆就暗下来的剧场

branches.en: a traveller running from a cry in the hills
branches.cn: 旅人听着山里的喊声拔腿就跑

branches.en: savers queuing outside a bank
branches.cn: 储户在银行门口排队

branches.en: a passenger searching for a lost passport
branches.cn: 乘客翻找丢失的护照

branches.en: shelves emptied and a crowd pushing at one door
branches.cn: 被扫空的货架与挤在同一扇门前的人群

intro.en: The word is a Greek name and phrase reshaped by Latin and French, and English then builds three more forms on the noun.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个希腊神名与短语，经拉丁语和法语改写，英语又在名词上造出三个形式。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin panicus is only a borrowing of Greek panikos, so no inherited Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 panicus 只是对希腊语 panikos 的借用，所以这个词没有可靠的拉丁固有同族词。

definition_zh: 游行；阅兵；炫耀；列队行进
definition_en: an organized public procession, a formal march of troops for inspection, a display meant to impress, and the act of marching in such a group
core_image: 彩旗在前，鼓点整齐，一条街被队伍填满
scene: 国庆那天的长街上，鼓乐队走在最前面，人群挤在两侧挥手。The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
sceneCN: 这里 parade 是「游行」（第 1 个义项：庆祝性的公众行进）；句意为全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。图中可辨识物件：彩旗、鼓、街道两侧的人群。

derivatives.zh: 由 parade 加 -ing 构成，指列队行进或刻意展示的行为

由 parade 与 ground 复合而成，指士兵操练、受阅的场地

senses.title: A public procession
senses.definition: an organized public march or procession, often with music, costumes and decorated vehicles, held to celebrate an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的公众行进，常配音乐、服装与彩车，用来庆祝某个日子
senses.example: The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。
senses.why: The word is generally traced through French to a Spanish noun for the place where soldiers halted and formed up; from troops gathering in the street it widened to any organized procession.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这个词经法语来自西班牙语中表示「士兵停下集合之处」的名词；从军队在街上集合，词义扩大为任何有组织的公众行进。

senses.title: A formal march of troops
senses.definition: a ceremony in which soldiers march in formation past a reviewing officer or a public stand
senses.definitionCN: 士兵列队走过检阅官或观礼台的仪式
senses.example: The general watched the parade from a raised platform.
senses.exampleCN: 将军站在检阅台上观看阅兵。
senses.why: Since the earliest parade was simply soldiers standing ready in one place, the military review is the oldest thread, and flags and formation still carry the sense of being inspected.
senses.whyCN: 既然最早的 parade 只是士兵在一处站好待命，阅兵就是最古老的一条线；旗帜与队形至今仍带着「接受检阅」的意味。

senses.title: A display meant to impress
senses.definition: an ostentatious show of wealth, skills or opinions intended to impress other people
senses.definitionCN: 为给人留下印象而摆出的财富、本领或主张
senses.example: His charity work was a parade of good intentions rather than real help.
senses.exampleCN: 他的慈善活动只是把好意摆出来给人看，并没有真正帮上忙。
senses.why: A procession exists to be watched, so when the watching matters more than the marching, the word slides into showing off.
senses.whyCN: 游行本来就是给人看的，一旦「被看见」比「行进」本身更重要，这个词就滑向了炫耀。

senses.title: To march in formation
senses.definition: to walk or march in an ordered group, especially as part of a ceremony or in order to be seen
senses.definitionCN: 排成整齐的队伍行走，尤指作为仪式的一部分或为了被人看见
senses.example: The children paraded around the playground with paper flags.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们举着纸旗在操场上列队走了一圈。
senses.why: The verb simply sets the procession moving: the same ordered line, now seen as an action instead of a spectacle.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是让那支队伍动起来：同样整齐的一列，从眼前的场面变成了正在进行的动作。

intro.en: Parade is usually traced through French to a Spanish noun for a halting place, with the Latin verb parare, to make ready, at the far end; the showy sense came later.
intro.cn: 一般认为 parade 经法语上溯到西班牙语中表示「停下之处」的名词，最远处是拉丁语动词 parare（准备、使就绪）；「炫耀」义出现得较晚。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or make ready, and its family spread through the Romance languages with senses of stopping and standing.
items.cn: parare 意为准备、使就绪，这一族词在罗曼语中扩散，带上停下、站定的意思。

items.en: Spanish parada named a halt or the place where troops stopped and formed up, from the verb parar, to stop.
items.cn: 西班牙语 parada 指停下的动作或士兵停下集合的地方，来自动词 parar（停下）。

items.en: French took the word as parade and used it for a setting out of troops and for a showy display.
items.cn: 法语借入后写作 parade，用来指军队列队出场，也指铺张的展示。

items.en: English borrowed parade for a military muster and for the ground where soldiers assembled.
items.cn: 英语借入 parade，指军队集合检阅，也指士兵集合的场地。

items.en: Modern English keeps the military review, the civic procession and the showy display, and uses the verb for marching and for showing off.
items.cn: 现代英语保留阅兵、市民游行与炫耀三层意思，动词则用于列队行进和炫耀。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Spanish and Latin words behind the term, plus two spellings that only resemble it; the near-meaning group follows processions, marches and displays.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个词背后的西班牙语与拉丁语词展开，另收两个只是拼写相像的词；近义组收游行、行进与展示。

entries.definition: A halt, or the place where troops stand ready; the Spanish noun behind the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 停下，或士兵站好待命之处；英语词背后的西班牙语名词。

entries.definition: To stop or to halt, the verb that produced the noun parada.
entries.definitionCN: 停下、止住，是造出名词 parada 的动词。

entries.definition: A comic imitation of a style or a work; it merely looks like parade and comes from other roots.
entries.definitionCN: 对某种风格或作品的滑稽模仿；只是拼写与 parade 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A typical example or a pattern of thinking; the spelling is close but the Greek roots are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 典型范例或思维模式；拼写相近，但希腊词根与 parade 无关。

entries.definition: A line of people or vehicles moving forward as part of a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 仪式中向前行进的一队人或车辆。

entries.definition: To walk with regular steps, especially as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 有节奏地行走，尤指成群行进。

entries.definition: A public show with costumes and scenes, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 常为户外的、带服装与场景的公众表演。

entries.definition: An arrangement or show intended to be looked at.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出来供人观看的展示。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a place where troops stood ready and became a line of people made to be watched; the family around it keeps those two ideas.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从士兵站好待命的地方开始，变成一列特意给人看的队伍；周围的词族一直带着这两个念头。

normal.en: The word is generally traced to Spanish parada, a halt where troops formed up, so the military sense is the oldest.
normal.cn: 一般认为这个词来自西班牙语 parada，即部队停下集合之处，所以军事义最古老。

normal.en: French parade added the idea of a show, which is why a fashion parade is about being watched rather than walking.
normal.cn: 法语 parade 加进了「展示」的意思，所以 fashion parade 的重点是被看，而不是走路。

normal.en: The verb is regular: parades, paraded, parading, with no change of vowel.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：parades、paraded、parading，元音不变。

normal.en: On parade means soldiers are lined up for inspection, not simply walking down a street.
normal.cn: on parade 指士兵列队接受检阅，并不是单纯在街上走。

normal.en: To rain on someone's parade is to spoil a moment that was arranged to be enjoyed in public.
normal.cn: rain on someone's parade 就是破坏一个本来要当众享受的时刻。

abstract.en: A parade turns a street into a stage, and everyone on it is at once performer and audience.
abstract.cn: 游行把街道变成舞台，走在上面的人既是演员也是观众。

abstract.en: A show of strength is still a show, and the word keeps that suspicion that display is not the same as substance.
abstract.cn: 力量的展示终究还是展示，这个词一直保留着「排场不等于实力」的疑虑。

abstract.en: Soldiers standing ready and a band walking past share one name because both are meant to be seen by someone in authority.
abstract.cn: 站好待命的士兵与走过的乐队共用一个词，因为两者都要让有权看的人看见。

examples.en: The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
examples.cn: 全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。

examples.en: The general watched the parade from a raised platform.
examples.cn: 将军站在检阅台上观看阅兵。

examples.en: The children paraded around the playground with paper flags.
examples.cn: 孩子们举着纸旗在操场上列队走了一圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕累的」——游行队伍走得太久也会怕累的；记住 parade 是游行。

root: 一般认为经法语 parade 来自西班牙语 parada（停下集合之处），源于拉丁语 parare（准备、使就绪）：士兵站好待命的地方，后来成了给人看的队伍。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an ordered line of people meant to be seen; the senses run from a civic celebration to a military review, to a showing off, and finally to the act of marching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一列特意给人看的整齐队伍；义项从市民庆祝走到阅兵、炫耀，最后落到列队行进这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band and a line of marchers filling the street while the crowd leans forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓乐队与一列行进的队伍占满街道，人群向前倾身观看。

branches.en: a band leading children down the main street
branches.cn: 鼓乐队带着孩子走过主街

branches.en: soldiers in step before a reviewing stand
branches.cn: 士兵在检阅台前齐步走过

branches.en: a borrowed car shown off at a party
branches.cn: 聚会上炫耀借来的车

branches.en: paper flags waving above a playground
branches.cn: 操场上挥动的纸旗

branches.en: boots striking the ground in one rhythm
branches.cn: 靴子以同一个节奏踏在地上

intro.en: The word is a Romance borrowing, and the pieces that built it are a Latin verb of preparing, a Spanish noun of halting, and a French noun of showing.
intro.cn: 这个词是罗曼语借词，构成它的部件是一个表示准备的拉丁动词、一个表示停下的西班牙名词和一个表示展示的法语名词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin verb is recorded behind this word: parare, to make ready, which passed into Spanish as parar and gave the noun parada.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有一个可考的拉丁动词 parare（准备、使就绪），它进入西班牙语成为 parar，并造出名词 parada。

definition_zh: 平行的；类似的；类似的事物；与……相似；与……同时发生
definition_en: of lines, always the same distance apart and never meeting; similar in important ways; a person or thing resembling another; to be similar to or to happen at the same time as
core_image: 两条铁轨并肩伸向远方，始终不碰在一起
scene: 两条铁轨穿过田野，一直伸到看不见的地方。The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
sceneCN: 这里 parallel 是「平行的」（第 1 个义项：两条线距离处处相同、永不相交）；句意为这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。图中可辨识物件：铁轨、枕木、远处的隧道口。

pos.zh: 类似的事物；可类比的对象

derivatives.zh: 由 parallel 加 -ism 构成，指平行、对应的状态，也指修辞上的排比
由 parallel 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed 构成，指无可比拟的
由 parallel 与希腊语 gramma（线）复合而成，指两组对边分别平行的四边形

senses.title: Always the same distance apart
senses.definition: of two or more lines or surfaces, keeping the same distance apart at every point so that they never meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条或多条线、面的距离处处相等，因而永不相交
senses.example: The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。
senses.why: Greek parallelos joins para, beside, with allelos, one another: two things set beside each other with an unbroken gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 parallelos 由 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此）拼成：两样东西彼此并排，中间隔着一道始终不变的距离。

senses.title: Similar in important ways
senses.definition: similar in a way that allows one thing to be compared with another, especially in structure or development
senses.definitionCN: 在结构或发展上相似到可以彼此对照
senses.example: The two cities followed parallel paths of growth after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后这两座城市走上了相似的发展道路。
senses.why: Lines that never meet still hold a constant relation, so the word came to name things that move in step without ever touching.
senses.whyCN: 永不相交的线仍保持固定的关系，于是这个词也用来指那些同步前进、却从不接触的事物。

senses.title: A person or thing like another
senses.titleCN: 类似的事物；可类比的对象
senses.definition: a person, event or situation that can be compared with another because of a clear resemblance
senses.definitionCN: 因为明显相像而可以拿来与另一者比较的人、事件或处境
senses.example: Historians drew a parallel between the two collapses.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这两次崩塌放在一起比较。
senses.why: Once the adjective names resemblance, the noun can name the second item itself, giving speakers a way to say that one thing is another's counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦表示相似，名词就能指那第二个对象本身，让人可以直说一件事是另一件事的对应物。

senses.title: To be similar to or happen alongside
senses.definition: to be similar to something, or to happen at the same time and in a connected way
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相似，或与它同时发生并彼此关联
senses.example: The rise in rents paralleled the growth of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨与这座城市的发展同步发生。
senses.why: The verb sets that picture in motion: two courses of events keep the same gap and move forward together.
senses.whyCN: 动词把那幅画面变成运动：两条事态的线索保持同样的间距，一起向前推进。

intro.en: Parallel comes from a Greek adjective meaning beside one another, built for geometry and later borrowed into Latin and English as a term of lines and likeness.
intro.cn: parallel 来自一个意为「彼此并排」的希腊形容词，本为几何学而造，后来被拉丁语与英语借用，用来指线与相似。

items.en: Parallelos joined para, beside, with allelos, one another, and described things set side by side at an even distance.
items.cn: parallelos 把 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此）拼在一起，描述以相等距离并排摆放的东西。

items.en: Greek geometers used the word for straight lines in one plane that never meet, and this technical sense has never been lost.
items.cn: 希腊几何学家用这个词指同一平面内永不相交的直线，这一专业义至今没有丢失。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as parallelus; it was a learned borrowing rather than a word inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 parallelus；这是学术借用，不是从拉丁语本土传下的词。

items.en: English took the word by way of Latin and French, first for geometry and soon after for any two things that resemble each other.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁语与法语借入这个词，先用于几何，随后很快用于任何彼此相像的两样东西。

items.en: Modern English keeps the geometrical sense, adds similarity and events running side by side, and uses the noun for a counterpart.
items.cn: 现代英语保留几何义，增加了相似与并行发生的意思，并用名词形式指对应物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other Greek compounds that begin with the same short element, each built on a different stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for likeness and for a matching thing.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以同一个短小成分开头的希腊复合词，每个词接的词干都不同；近义组收表示相似以及对应物的词。

entries.definition: Greek para plus graphein, to write; the prefix looks the same but the formation is separate, not a shared family.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 graphein（写）；前缀写法相同，但构词各自独立，不是同一词族。

entries.definition: Para beside plus doxa opinion, a claim that runs against common belief.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 doxa（意见），指违背常见看法的说法。

entries.definition: Para beside plus sitos food, one who eats at another person's table.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 sitos（食物），指在别人桌边吃饭的寄生者。

entries.definition: Greek para plus allassein, to change; it shares the all- element with parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 allassein（改变）；与 parallel 共享 all- 这一成分。

entries.definition: Almost the same, but not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎相同，但并不完全一样。

entries.definition: Similar in a way that allows a comparison between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 相似到可以把两者放在一起比较。

entries.definition: A person or thing that has the same role as another elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处担任同一角色的人或事物。

entries.definition: Next to and parallel with something.
entries.definitionCN: 在旁边并与某物并排。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek picture of two things laid side by side, and the whole family keeps the ideas of even distance, likeness and a matching partner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语里两样东西并排放置的画面，整族词都带着等距、相似与配对这三层意思。

normal.en: The Greek parts are para, beside, and allelos, one another, so parallel lines are lines placed beside each other.
normal.cn: 希腊部件是 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此），所以平行线就是彼此并排放着的线。

normal.en: The same picture yields the sense of similar: two courses stay side by side without ever meeting.
normal.cn: 同一幅画面也生出「相似」：两条走向并排前进，却始终不相交。

normal.en: Parallel ends in -el with one r, while parallelism adds -ism and keeps the same l-sound.
normal.cn: parallel 以一个 r、结尾 -el 拼写，parallelism 则加 -ism，l 音不变。

normal.en: In parallel means two things are running at the same time, like two tracks carrying trains.
normal.cn: in parallel 指两件事同时进行，就像两条各跑列车的轨道。

normal.en: The verb is regular: parallels, paralleled, paralleling, with the final l doubled.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：parallels、paralleled、paralleling，末尾的 l 双写。

abstract.en: Parallel lines are a promise that two things can stay close forever without ever becoming one.
abstract.cn: 平行线是一种承诺：两样东西可以永远靠得很近，却始终不合成一个。

abstract.en: To draw a parallel is to say that two separate stories are running on the same track.
abstract.cn: 把两者作类比，就是说两个互不相干的故事跑在同一条轨道上。

abstract.en: A parallel universe is the everyday metaphor for a life that kept the same distance from this one.
abstract.cn: 平行宇宙是日常语言里对「另一种人生」的比喻：它与这一种人生始终隔着同样的距离。

examples.en: The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
examples.cn: 这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。

examples.en: The two cities followed parallel paths of growth after the war.
examples.cn: 战后这两座城市走上了相似的发展道路。

examples.en: The rise in rents paralleled the growth of the city.
examples.cn: 租金的上涨与这座城市的发展同步发生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「排啊排」——两条线一直排着走，谁也不碰谁；记住 parallel 是平行。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁边）加 allelos（彼此）构成 parallelos，指彼此并排、距离相等的线；经中世纪拉丁语 parallelus 与法语进入英语。它与 paragraph 虽然同写 para-，但接的词干不同，是两套独立的构词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things laid side by side at a fixed distance; the senses move from geometry to resemblance, to a matching partner, and to events that run alongside each other.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是以固定距离并排放置的两样东西；义项从几何走到相似，再到对应物，最后是并行发生的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rails shining toward a tunnel mouth, never touching.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条铁轨闪着光伸向隧道口，始终不相碰。

branches.en: two rails shining toward a tunnel mouth
branches.cn: 两条铁轨亮着伸向隧道口

branches.en: two trains holding the same gap on twin tracks
branches.cn: 两列火车在平行轨道上保持同样的间距

branches.en: two cities growing along the same pattern
branches.cn: 两座城市沿同样的模式生长

branches.en: a historian placing two collapses side by side
branches.cn: 历史学家把两次崩塌并排比较

branches.en: rents and population climbing together on a chart
branches.cn: 租金与人口在图表上一同上升

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound of a preposition and a pronoun meaning one another, and English suffixes then build the nouns and adjectives around it.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中一个介词与意为「彼此」的代词拼成的复合词，英语后缀随后在它周围造出名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; medieval Latin parallelus is a learned borrowing of the Greek adjective, so the Latin form follows the Greek rather than feeding it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；中世纪拉丁语的 parallelus 是对希腊形容词的学术借用，拉丁形式是跟着希腊语走的，而非其来源。

definition_zh: 包裹；邮包；一块土地；把……包起来；分派
definition_en: something wrapped in paper or packed in a box and sent by post, a measured area of land, or to wrap goods and divide them into portions
core_image: 柜台上一只牛皮纸包被麻绳捆成十字，收件地址写在正面
scene: 邮局柜台前，店员把一只用麻绳捆好的纸包推过来，又把票据压在下面。He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
sceneCN: 这里的 parcel 是「包裹、邮包」（第 1 个义项：包好待寄送的东西）；句意是他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。图中可辨识物件：麻绳、牛皮纸包、票据。

derivatives.zh: 由 parcel 双写 l 加 -ing 构成，义为「打包；分块的方式」
由 parcel 与 post 复合而成，义为「包裹邮政」
由 parcel 与 bomb 复合而成，义为「邮包炸弹」

senses.title: Something wrapped and sent by post
senses.definition: something wrapped in paper, tied with string or packed in a box, especially for sending by post
senses.definitionCN: 用纸包好、用绳捆上或装进盒子，尤指通过邮局寄送的东西
senses.example: He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
senses.exampleCN: 他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。
senses.why: Parcel began as Latin particula, a small part, and French used it for a small piece of anything; an item tied up for the post was simply one such piece.
senses.whyCN: parcel 最初是拉丁语 particula，意为「一小部分」，法语用它指任何东西的一小块；寄送时捆好的那件东西，不过是这样的「一块」而已。

senses.title: A measured piece of land
senses.definition: a piece of land, especially one marked out for a particular use or owned as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 一块土地，尤指划作某种用途或作为一个单位拥有的地块
senses.example: They bought a small parcel of land beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边买下了一小块地。
senses.why: If a parcel is a portion cut from a whole, land can be divided the same way, so the word came to name one plot marked on a surveyor's map.
senses.whyCN: 既然 parcel 是从整体里切出的一份，土地也能这样切分，于是这个词用来指测量图上标好的一个地块。

senses.title: To wrap something up
senses.definition: to wrap goods in paper or another material and fasten them, often before sending
senses.definitionCN: 把货物用纸或其他材料包好并捆紧，通常是为了寄送
senses.example: She parcelled the books and took them to the post office.
senses.exampleCN: 她把书包好，送到邮局去。
senses.why: The noun named the finished bundle, so the verb simply names the act of producing it: to parcel is to turn loose goods into one tied package.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是包好的成品，动词便直接指做出这个成品的动作：parcel 就是把散着的东西变成一只捆好的包。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.definition: to divide something into portions and give them out, usually in the phrase parcel out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份分发出去，通常用于 parcel out 这一说法
senses.example: The land was parcelled out among the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地被分给了村民们。
senses.why: Because the word already meant a portion, parcel out reverses the picture: instead of gathering things into one bundle, it cuts the whole into separate shares.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就指「一份」，parcel out 于是把画面翻了过来：不再把东西收进一只包，而是把整体切成一份份拿出去。

intro.en: Parcel comes from Old French parcelle, a small piece, which is a diminutive of Latin particula, itself a small form of pars, part; English first used it for a portion and only later for a package and a plot of land.
intro.cn: parcel 来自古法语 parcelle（一小块），它是拉丁语 particula 的指小形式，而 particula 又是 pars（部分）的小称；英语先用它指「一份」，后来才指包裹与地块。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and it is the ultimate source of a whole family of English words about portions.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，是英语中一整族表示「份」的词的最终来源。

items.en: Particula was the small form of pars, so it named a little part or a tiny piece of something.
items.cn: particula 是 pars 的小称，指一小部分或某物的一小块。

items.en: Old French kept the word as parcelle and used it for a small piece or a portion of a larger whole.
items.cn: 古法语把它保留为 parcelle，用来指一小块或整体中的一份。

items.en: Middle English parcel first meant a part or a portion, and it could name a piece of land as well as a share of goods.
items.cn: 中古英语的 parcel 最初指部分或一份，既能指一块地，也能指一份货物。

items.en: Modern English made the wrapped item the main sense, kept the land sense, and added the verb meanings of wrapping and dividing.
items.cn: 现代英语把包好的东西变成主要义项，保留土地义，又添上「包起来」与「分成份」两个动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin root for part, so the split between parcel and the partial family is visible; the near-meaning group gathers words for wrapped goods.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「部分」词根上的词，方便看清 parcel 与 partial 一族的分叉；近义组收表示包好的货物的词。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; both words descend from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；两个词都出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: Covering only a part, or favouring one side; from Latin pars.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的，或偏袒一方的；出自拉丁语 pars。

entries.definition: One specific thing rather than any other; from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的那一个，而不是别的；出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: To take a share of something, as in partake of a meal.
entries.definitionCN: 分享一份，如 partake of a meal 指一同进餐。

entries.definition: Something wrapped or boxed, especially for sending or selling.
entries.definitionCN: 包好或装箱的东西，尤指寄送或出售的。

entries.definition: A small paper or plastic container holding a measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 装一定量物品的纸或塑料小袋。

entries.definition: A number of things tied or wrapped together.
entries.definitionCN: 捆在一起或包在一起的一堆东西。

entries.definition: A load of goods sent to someone, especially for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 发运给某人的一批货物，尤指出售用。

normalIntro.en: Parcel is a word for a piece cut from a whole, and its hooks follow that piece from a share of land to a bundle tied for the post.
normalIntro.cn: parcel 是一个表示「从整体中切下的一块」的词，记忆钩子顺着这块东西，从一份土地走到捆好待寄的包裹。

normal.en: Parcel descends from Latin pars, part, through particula and Old French parcelle, so a parcel is literally a little part.
normal.cn: parcel 经由 particula 与古法语 parcelle 上溯拉丁语 pars（部分），所以它字面上就是「一小块」。

normal.en: A parcel of land keeps the oldest sense visible: a measured share of ground, not a thing you mail.
normal.cn: a parcel of land 保留了最古老的义项：量好的一份地，而不是寄出去的东西。

normal.en: Parcel out reverses the picture of a tied bundle: the whole is cut into portions instead of being gathered into one.
normal.cn: parcel out 把捆成一只包的画面翻了过来：整体被切成若干份，而不是被收进一只包。

normal.en: Part and parcel uses the old sense of a share to say that something is an inseparable piece of a larger thing.
normal.cn: part and parcel 用的是「一份」的旧义，表示某物是更大整体中不可分割的一块。

normal.en: The British verb doubles the l as parcelled, while the American spelling keeps one l as parceled.
normal.cn: 英式动词双写 l 写作 parcelled，美式拼写只留一个 l，写作 parceled。

abstract.en: A word that means both a mailed package and a plot of land suggests that owning and sending are both matters of pieces.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指邮寄的包裹又指一块地，说明拥有与投递都与「份」有关。

abstract.en: Because parcel began as a small part, every parcel still carries the idea of a whole that has been divided.
abstract.cn: 因为 parcel 起初指一小部分，所以每一只包裹至今都带着「整体被分割过」的意思。

abstract.en: To parcel out land or money is to admit that a whole cannot stay whole once it belongs to several people.
abstract.cn: 把土地或钱分派出去，等于承认整体一旦归几个人所有，就再也无法保持完整。

examples.en: He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
examples.cn: 他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。

examples.en: They bought a small parcel of land beside the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边买下了一小块地。

examples.en: The land was parcelled out among the villagers.
examples.cn: 这块地被分给了村民们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕搜」——邮局里的人怕搜，先把东西捆成一包再递出去；记住 parcel 是包裹，也指一块地。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）经小称 particula 与古法语 parcelle 进入英语；同族有 particle、partial、particular，词义从「一小份」分叉出「包好的一件」「一块地」「分成份」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a piece cut from a whole; the senses divide into the piece tied for the post, the piece of ground, the act of wrapping, and the act of dividing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从整体中切下的一块；义项按「捆好待寄的那一件」「一块地」「包起来的动作」「分成份的动作」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown paper parcel crossed by string, an address written on the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只牛皮纸包被麻绳捆成十字，正面写着收件地址。

branches.cn: 从邮局柜台上推过来的一只包裹

branches.en: an address in ink on brown paper
branches.cn: 牛皮纸上用墨水写下的地址

branches.en: a strip of riverside field marked on a map
branches.cn: 地图上标出的河边一条田地

branches.en: string pulled tight and knotted around paper
branches.cn: 绳子在纸上拉紧打结

branches.en: a field cut into narrow strips for several families
branches.cn: 一块地被切成细条分给几户人家

intro.en: Latin pars and its small form particula supply the meaning of a piece, French passes the word on, and two English suffixes build the noun and the action.
intro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 及其小称 particula 提供「一块」的含义，法语把词传给英语，两个英语后缀再把它变成名词与动作。

latinIntro.en: Both Latin pars and particula are recorded, so this word has a reliable Latin ancestry shared with particle, partial and particular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 与 particula 均有记录，因此这个词有可靠的拉丁世系，并与 particle、partial、particular 同源。

definition_zh: 原谅；饶恕；赦免；（礼貌用语）请再说一遍
definition_en: to forgive someone or officially free them from punishment; a polite word asking someone to repeat
core_image: 松开惩罚的手：本要落下的责罚被收了回去
scene: 听到同桌小声嘀咕了一句没听清，他放下了手中的笔。"Pardon? Could you say that again?" he asked politely.
sceneCN: 这里 pardon 是「（礼貌地）请再说一遍」（第 4 个义项）；句意是他没听清，礼貌地请对方重复一遍。

derivatives.zh: 由 pardon 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可原谅的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pardonable 构成，义为「不可原谅的」
由 pardon 加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「给予原谅（赦免）的人」

senses.title: To forgive an offence
senses.definition: to forgive someone for a fault or wrong they have done
senses.definitionCN: 原谅某人所犯的过失或错误
senses.example: He begged her pardon for arriving so late.
senses.exampleCN: 他为自己迟到这么久请求她的原谅。
senses.why: The core image is withdrawing the hand of punishment; forgiving means pulling back the penalty.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是收回惩罚之手；原谅就是把将要落下的责罚收回去。

senses.title: To officially free from legal punishment
senses.definition: to officially allow someone who has been convicted of a crime to go free or be released from punishment
senses.definitionCN: 官方正式免除被定罪者的刑罚或准予其免受处罚
senses.example: The governor granted a full pardon to the wrongly convicted man.
senses.exampleCN: 州长对蒙冤定罪的男子颁布了完全赦免。
senses.why: The legal sense keeps the same image: the state withdraws a punishment already decided.
senses.whyCN: 法律义项保留同一画面：国家收回已经判定的惩罚。

senses.title: A polite way to say sorry
senses.titleCN: 抱歉；（引起注意或致歉的礼貌语）
senses.definition: a polite expression used to say sorry or to get someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 表示歉意或引起对方注意的礼貌用语
senses.example: "Pardon me," he said, as he squeezed past the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 「借过一下，」他说着挤过人群。
senses.why: Asking pardon literally means asking to be forgiven for a small disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 说 pardon me 字面上就是请求对方原谅自己小小的打扰。

senses.title: A polite request to repeat
senses.definition: a polite question asking someone to repeat what they said, often because you did not hear it
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请对方重复刚才的话，常因没听清
senses.example: "Pardon? I didn't catch your name," she said.
senses.exampleCN: 「您再说一遍好吗？我没听清您的名字，」她说。
senses.why: In British English, rising pardon politely asks the speaker to try again.
senses.whyCN: 在英式英语中，语调上扬的 pardon 礼貌地请对方再说一次。

intro.en: Pardon travelled from Latin through Old French into English, always built on the idea of giving completely and fairly.
intro.cn: pardon 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，词义始终建立在「完全而公正地给予」这一根义之上。

items.en: The root is perdonare: per- (completely, thoroughly) plus donare (to give), literally "to give wholeheartedly".
items.cn: 词根是拉丁语 perdonare：per-（完全地）加 donare（给予），字面义为「全心全意地给予」。

items.en: Old French pardonner meant to grant, to forgive, and to remit a punishment.
items.cn: 古法语 pardonner 意为给予、宽恕、免除惩罚。

items.en: In medieval church use, perdonare and related forms covered the remission of sins and penalties.
items.cn: 在中世纪教会语境中，perdonare 及相关形式用于表示赦罪与减免惩罚。

items.en: Modern French keeps pardon as both the forgiveness noun and the everyday "sorry" expression.
items.cn: 现代法语中 pardon 既是「宽恕」名词，也是日常表示「抱歉」的用语。

items.en: English took the word from Old French in the 13th century, first in the legal and religious senses.
items.cn: 英语于十三世纪从古法语借入该词，最早用于法律与宗教语境。

items.en: Later uses extended it to polite apologies and the request to repeat a sentence.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它扩展为礼貌致歉语和请对方重复的用语。

note.en: Pardon shares a family with forgive and excuse; the words below are its close neighbours.
note.cn: pardon 与 forgive、excuse 同属一个词族；下列词是它的近邻。

entries.definition: able to be forgiven
entries.definitionCN: 可原谅的；pardon 的形容词派生词

entries.definition: too serious to be forgiven
entries.definitionCN: 不可原谅的；加否定前缀 un- 的派生词

entries.definition: a person who grants pardons or forgiveness
entries.definitionCN: 赦免者；宽恕者；pardon 的名词派生词

entries.definition: made hard or unfeeling; only the ending resembles pardon
entries.definitionCN: 变硬的；冷酷的；词尾拼写相近但词源完全不同

entries.definition: to stop being angry about a fault; general everyday forgiving
entries.definitionCN: 原谅；泛指日常的不计前嫌，语气比 pardon 更温厚

entries.definition: to overlook a small fault or politely allow something
entries.definitionCN: 宽恕；原谅小的过失，也用于礼貌套语 excuse me

entries.definition: to declare in court that someone is not guilty
entries.definitionCN: 宣判无罪；pardon 是事后赦免，acquit 是判决定罪前的开释

entries.definition: an official act of forgiving a group of offenders together
entries.definitionCN: 大赦； amnesty 面向群体，pardon 通常面向个人

normalIntro.en: Break the word into its Latin parts and reuse it in polite phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成拉丁成分，并在礼貌用语中反复使用。

normal.en: par- (completely) + don (give): to give completely is to forgive completely.
normal.cn: par-（完全地）加 don（给予）：完全地给予，就是彻底地原谅。

normal.en: don is the give root, the same one as in donate.
normal.cn: don 是「给予」词根，与 donate（捐赠）中的 don 相同。

normal.en: I beg your pardon = I beg your giving-back of the punishment.
normal.cn: I beg your pardon 字面是「恳求您收回责罚」。

normal.en: Pardon my French: pardon me for the rude words.
normal.cn: Pardon my French：为我刚才的粗话求个原谅。

normal.en: In French, pardon itself means sorry — the polite use came straight across.
normal.cn: 法语里 pardon 本身就是「抱歉」，礼貌用法直接从法语移植。

abstract.en: Picture a judge's raised hand slowly lowering: the punishment never falls.
abstract.cn: 想象法官举起的手缓缓放下：惩罚始终没有落下。

abstract.en: A governor signs one paper and a prisoner walks free.
abstract.cn: 州长签下一纸赦令，囚徒从此自由。

abstract.en: You cup your ear: "Pardon?" — asking the sound to come again.
abstract.cn: 你拢起耳朵说「请再说一遍」，恳请那句话重来一次。

examples.en: She pardoned his rudeness, knowing he had been under stress.
examples.cn: 她原谅了他的无礼，知道他一直压力很大。

examples.en: The president granted a pardon to the former prisoner.
examples.cn: 总统对这名前囚徒颁布了赦免。

examples.en: "Pardon?" he asked, leaning closer to hear the announcement.
examples.cn: 「您能再说一遍吗？」他凑近去听广播。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕等」——pardon 谐音「怕等」：求人原谅的人最「怕等」，怕对方不肯收回责罚；听到没听清也「怕等」不了，赶紧说句 pardon 请对方再说一遍。

root: pardon 源自拉丁语 perdonare，由 per-（完全地）与 donare（给予）构成，字面义为「全心全意地给予」；经古法语 pardonner 于十三世纪进入英语，词义由「宽恕」扩展到「赦免」与礼貌套语。

sensesIntro.en: From forgiving a personal wrong, pardon widens to official remission of punishment, then narrows into polite formulas for apology and for asking a speaker to repeat.
sensesIntro.cn: 从原谅个人过错出发，pardon 扩展到官方赦免刑罚，再收窄为致歉与请人复述的礼貌用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: withdrawing the hand of punishment
core.cn: 核心意象：收回即将落下的惩罚之手

branches.en: Forgiving a personal fault
branches.cn: 原谅个人的过失

branches.en: Officially releasing someone from legal punishment
branches.cn: 正式赦免刑罚

branches.en: Polite apology for a small disturbance
branches.cn: 为小打扰致歉

branches.en: Politely asking for a sentence to be repeated
branches.cn: 礼貌请求复述

branches.en: Everyday formulas built on asking forgiveness
branches.cn: 建立在求恕之上的日常套语

intro.en: The per- plus don- skeleton explains both the meaning and the family of pardon words.
intro.cn: per- 加 don- 的骨架既解释了词义，也串起了 pardon 词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root donare, to give, also produced donate, donor, and donation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 donare（给予）还派生出 donate、donor、donation 等词。

items.example: Perform means to carry something through completely.
items.exampleCN: perform 的 per- 表示彻底完成。

items.example: That was a pardonable mistake for a beginner.
items.exampleCN: 对初学者来说那是可原谅的错误。

items.example: Betting away the rent was unpardonable.
items.exampleCN: 把房租拿去赌博是不可原谅的。

items.example: Only the president is the pardoner in that case.
items.exampleCN: 在那类案件中只有总统有权赦免。

items.example: They donate books to the village school every year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年向村校捐赠图书。

items.example: The anonymous donor paid for the library.
items.exampleCN: 匿名捐赠者出资修建了图书馆。

items.meaning: to overlook or forgive an offence
items.example: The school does not condone cheating.

definition_zh: 议会；国会；（英国的）议会；（一届全国议会的）任期
definition_en: the national lawmaking assembly of a country, especially one in which the government is drawn from its members
core_image: 一间圆形大厅里两排长凳相对而坐，中间的地毯上放着一份待辩的文件
scene: 圆形大厅里两排长凳相对，中间的地毯上摊着一份文件。Parliament debated the bill until midnight.
sceneCN: 句中这个词指一国的国家立法议会，尤其指政府由议员产生的体制（第 1 个义项：由民选代表组成、掌握立法权的国家议会）；句意为议会辩论该法案直到午夜。图中可辨识物件：两排长凳、中央地毯、文件、议长席位、表决通道；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 一届议会的任期；议会会议时期

senses.title: A national lawmaking assembly
senses.definition: the supreme lawmaking body of a state, especially where the executive answers to it
senses.definitionCN: 一国的最高立法机构，尤指行政须向它负责的体制
senses.example: Parliament debated the bill until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 议会辩论该法案直到午夜。
senses.why: The word first meant a talking together, and the national assembly is the place where the talking decides law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「一起说话」，而国家议会就是说话决定法律的地方。

senses.title: The building
senses.definition: the building or chamber where the assembly meets
senses.definitionCN: 议会开会所在的建筑或议事厅
senses.example: A crowd gathered outside parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 一群人聚集在议会大厦外。
senses.why: By metonymy the place takes the name of the body that meets in it.
senses.whyCN: 借代作用使地点取得了在其中开会之机构的名字。

senses.title: The members collectively
senses.definition: the assembled members considered as one actor
senses.definitionCN: 把全体议员视为一个行动者
senses.example: Parliament was divided on the question.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在这个问题上意见分裂。
senses.why: A body acts through votes, so the name passes from the institution to the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 机构通过投票行动，于是名称从制度转到里面的人。

senses.title: A term or session
senses.definition: the period between one general election and the next, or a single session
senses.definitionCN: 两次大选之间的一段时期，或一次会期
senses.example: The law was passed in the last parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律在上一届议会任期内通过。
senses.why: Because the assembly is dissolved and reconstituted, the word also counts the periods of its life.
senses.whyCN: 由于议会被解散又重新组成，这个词也用来数它生命的周期。

senses.title: A medieval council
senses.titleCN: 中世纪由君主召集的会议
senses.definition: a conference of nobles and clergy summoned by a monarch to advise and consent
senses.definitionCN: 由君主召集、由贵族与教士提供建议并同意的会议
senses.example: The medieval parliament began as a royal council.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的议会起初是王室会议。
senses.why: Before it made law, the assembly was a speaking-together called by the king, and that is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 在制定法律之前，这个集会是由国王召集的「一起说话」，那是最老的义项。

senses.title: A regional or supranational parliament
senses.definition: a lawmaking or deliberative assembly below or above the national level
senses.definitionCN: 低于或高于国家层级的立法或议事议会
senses.example: The Scottish Parliament sits in Edinburgh.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰议会设在爱丁堡。
senses.why: Once the model exists, it can be copied at any level, from a province to a continent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了这个模式，它就能被复制到任何层级，从一省到一洲。

senses.title: Any deliberative assembly
senses.definition: an extended use for a meeting that argues out a decision
senses.definitionCN: 引申用法，指通过争论作出决定的会议
senses.example: The students held a parliament on the library steps.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在图书馆台阶上开了一场议事会。
senses.why: Talking toward a decision is the original action, so the label travels to any group that does it.
senses.whyCN: 为了决定而说话是原本的动作，因此这个标签能转到任何这样做的群体。

senses.title: A literary gathering
senses.titleCN: 文学中的群鸟议事（典故）
senses.definition: the title word of medieval poems in which birds or beasts hold a council
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪诗题中的用词，写群鸟或群兽开会
senses.example: Chaucer's poem is known as the Parliament of Fowls.
senses.exampleCN: 乔叟那首诗被称为《百鸟议会》。
senses.why: The poem takes the assembly's name and applies it to birds, which is the word's most playful reach.
senses.whyCN: 这首诗借用了议会的名字，把它用在鸟身上，是这个词汇最俏皮的延伸。

intro.en: Parliament comes from Old French parlement, first 'a speaking, talk' and then 'a conference'. The verb parler 'to speak' goes back through Late Latin parabolare to parabola 'speech, comparison', from Greek parabole.
intro.cn: parliament 来自古法语 parlement，最初意为「说话、谈话」，后指「会议」。动词 parler「说话」经晚期拉丁 parabolare 上溯到 parabola「言语、比较」，再上溯到希腊语 parabole。

items.en: Parabole meant a placing beside, hence a comparison and a story used as a comparison. It passed into Latin as parabola.
items.cn: parabole 意为「放在旁边」，因此指比较，也指用作比较的故事。它进入拉丁语作 parabola。

items.en: The verb parabolare 'to speak, talk' grew out of parabola in late and vulgar Latin, and from it came French parler.
items.cn: 动词 parabolare「说话、谈话」在晚期与通俗拉丁语中由 parabola 长出，法语 parler 即由此而来。

items.en: Parlement named a speaking or a conference before it named an institution; the Anglo-Latin form parliamentum is recorded from the early thirteenth century.
items.cn: parlement 先指说话或会谈，后指机构；其盎格鲁拉丁形式 parliamentum 自十三世纪早期见于记录。

items.en: English parliament is recorded about 1300 for a formal conference, and by the mid-fourteenth century for the representative assembly of England.
items.cn: 英语 parliament 约在 1300 年指正式会议，到十四世纪中期指英格兰的代表性议会。

items.en: The spelling was altered about 1400 to match Medieval Latin parliamentum, which is why the word has an i that the French form lacks.
